title: Drop machine states
statement: A drop-machine state is one of the following: a length test or length increment; a copy state with a stage in $\{0,\ldots,7\}$ and a Boolean flag; a scan or first state with a layer in $\{0,1,2\}$; a second or second-read state with such a layer and a Boolean flag; a scan-increment state with a layer and two indices in $\{0,1,2,3\}$; a tail-test state with a Boolean flag, or one of the tail-check, tail-read, or tail-done states; a tail-half or tail-increment state with a Boolean flag; a pointer-clearing state with a stage in $\{0,1,2,3,4\}$; a $z$-decrement state with a step in $\{0,1\}$, or a $u$-decrement state with a step in $\{0,1,2,3\}$; one of the decode, decode-down, or decode-read states; a decode-copy, decode-copy-increment, decode-clear, decode-scale, decode-take, or decode-add state with a Boolean flag; a decode-increment state with two Boolean flags; a seek, match-index, or next-index state with a Boolean flag; a walk state with a Boolean flag and a step in $\{0,1,2,3\}$; a hit state; or an answer state with a Boolean flag.
